name: Healthy foliage
care: Keep the current watering and feeding routine.
Keep inspecting weekly so problems are caught early.

name: Early blight (Alternaria)
signs: brown spots with concentric rings like a target
care: Remove and destroy affected lower leaves.
Water at the soil, not over the leaves, and mulch to stop soil splash.
Rotate crops; use a labelled fungicide (copper or chlorothalonil) if it spreads.

name: Target spot (Corynespora)
signs: small brown spots that enlarge with faint concentric rings
spots on leaves, stems and fruit
care: Remove infected leaves and improve airflow between plants.
Avoid long periods of wet leaves.
Use a labelled fungicide if many leaves are affected.

name: Late blight (Phytophthora infestans)
signs: large irregular grey-green to dark brown patches
white fuzzy growth on the underside in humid weather
care: Remove and destroy infected plants; do not compost them.
Keep leaves dry and space plants for airflow.
Protect healthy plants with a labelled fungicide; act quickly, it spreads within days.

name: Septoria leaf spot
signs: grey or tan centres with dark borders
tiny black dots in the centre
care: Remove affected lower leaves.
Avoid overhead watering and mulch the soil.
Rotate crops and use a labelled fungicide if needed.

name: Bacterial spot (Xanthomonas)
signs: small dark brown to black water-soaked spots
spots may have a yellow halo
spots merge and leaves turn yellow
care: Remove badly affected leaves; do not work with plants when they are wet.
Avoid overhead watering.
Use disease-free seed; copper sprays can slow spread.

name: Leaf mould (Passalora fulva)
signs: pale green or yellow patches on the upper leaf surface
olive-green to brown velvety mould on the underside
care: Lower humidity and improve ventilation.
Remove affected leaves.
Water early in the day so leaves dry quickly.

name: Powdery mildew
signs: white or grey powdery coating on leaves
usually starts on upper leaf surfaces
care: Remove affected leaves and improve airflow.
Avoid excess nitrogen fertiliser.
Sulphur or potassium bicarbonate sprays can control it.

name: Spider mites
signs: fine yellow or white speckling (stippling) on leaves
care: Spray the leaf undersides with water to knock mites off.
Use insecticidal soap or neem oil.
Avoid drought stress, which favours mites.

name: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus
care: There is no cure: remove infected plants.
Control whiteflies (yellow sticky traps, insect netting).
Use resistant varieties next season.

name: Mosaic virus
signs: light and dark green mottled mosaic pattern
care: There is no cure: remove infected plants.
Wash hands and tools; the virus spreads by touch.
Control aphids and use resistant varieties.

name: Nitrogen deficiency
signs: even yellowing of older lower leaves first
care: Apply a balanced or nitrogen-rich fertiliser.
Add compost to the soil.
Recheck in 1 to 2 weeks for new green growth.

name: Water stress (underwatering)
signs: wilting or drooping in dry soil
care: Water deeply, then let the topsoil dry slightly between waterings.
Mulch to keep moisture in.
Check soil moisture before watering.

name: Overwatering / root rot
signs: wilting even though the soil is wet
soft dark stem base or roots
care: Water less often and only when the topsoil is dry.
Improve drainage.
Check roots: remove soft, dark roots.
